payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1, every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, and every real t with 0 <= t < 1, one has floor(n*t) = m if and only if m/n <= t < (m+1)/n.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1, an integer m with 0<=m<=n-1, and a real t with 0<=t<1. We prove that floor(n t)=m if and only if m/n<=t<(m+1)/n.

By the defining property of the floor function, for any real y and any integer m one has floor(y)=m exactly when m<=y<m+1. Apply this with y=n t. Then
floor(n t)=m  iff  m<=n t<m+1.

Since n>1, in particular n>0. Dividing the displayed inequalities by the positive number n preserves their directions, so
m<=n t<m+1  iff  m/n<=t<(m+1)/n.

Combining the two equivalences gives
floor(n t)=m  iff  m/n<=t<(m+1)/n.
This is exactly the claimed statement.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the standard characterization of the floor function and divide the inequality by the positive integer n.

used_external_facts: Standard characterization of the floor function: floor(y)=m iff m<=y<m+1
